name: Research Project & Core Semiannual Progress Report
intro_text: Upload a 2–3 page Word document covering your accomplishments, your plans for the next period, and any changes. Name it with your last name and what it is, for example Cain_Accomplishments.

about: Your semi-annual progress report summarizes your accomplishments, plans and changes.
It feeds directly into the Center’s progress report to NIH.

sections.title: Accomplishments
sections.instructions:
Your document should contain the following:
- Activities
- Objectives
- Significant Results
- Key Outcomes
- Unmet Goals

For Projects:
- What experiments you completed (give reference to aims/milestones/timeline)
- What you found
- Dissemination of Information

For Cores:
- Implementations of renovations, building of core
- Core activity and use

sections.title: Plans
sections.instructions:
Provide a summary of what you plan to do during the next reporting period to accomplish your project goals and objectives. Discuss efforts to ensure that the approach continues to be scientifically rigorous and results are robust and unbiased.
Remember that significant changes in objectives and scope require prior approval of the agency (e.g., NIH Grants Policy Statement, 8.1.2.). Include any important modifications to the original plans. Provide a scientific justification for any changes involving research with human subjects or vertebrate animals. A detailed description of such changes must be provided under Changes.

sections.title: Changes
sections.instructions: Describe challenges or delays encountered during the reporting period and actions or plans to resolve them. Describe only significant challenges that may impede the research (e.g., accrual of patients, hiring of personnel, need for resources or research tools) and emphasize their resolution.

sections.title: Evidence of Esteem
sections.instructions: Please give evidence of esteem in your uploaded document. Examples are invited talks and service on review panels or editorial boards.

questions.help_text: Please upload your file here. Word documents only (.docx or .doc).

sections.title: Quick RPPR questions
sections.instructions: NIH asks these for each project and core every year. Most answers are No.

questions.prompt: B.1.a Have the major goals changed since the initial competing award or previous report?
C.3 Did this work produce new technologies or techniques during this reporting period?
C.4 Did it produce inventions, patent applications or licenses during this reporting period?
C.5.a Did it produce other significant products, such as databases, software, models or instruments?
C.5.c Is data from this work being shared as its Data Management and Sharing plan describes?
F.3 Were there significant changes to human subjects, vertebrate animals, biohazards or select agents?
G.9 Was any significant part of this work done outside the United States, or by someone employed by a foreign organization?
Details for each Yes above, and for a No on C.5.c. Start each note with the item, like “C.4: …”.

sections.title: Research team (RPPR D.1)
sections.instructions:
List everyone who worked on this project or core during this budget year, including you. Use one row per person.
Give effort in person months: calendar months for 12-month appointments, or academic and summer months for 9-month appointments.

questions.prompt: eRA Commons ID (if they have one)
Role on this project or core

sections.title: Suggested RPPR tables (optional)
sections.instructions: If the Center sent you RPPR tables to fill in, such as B.1 goals or G.1, upload them here instead of emailing them.
